 220|## 8. Risk Assessment
 221|
 222|| Risk | Probability | Impact | Mitigation | Contingency |
 223||------|-------------|--------|------------|-------------|
 224|| Code injection via eval() | low | high | Use safe parsing algorithm (shunting-yard) and never use eval() or exec(). | If eval() is accidentally used, revert to safe parser and conduct code review. |
 225|| Denial of service via long input | medium | high | Enforce maximum input length of 1000 characters and limit recursion depth. | If DoS occurs, implement input length check and timeout mechanism. |
 226|| Input injection via special characters | medium | medium | Whitelist-based input validation: only allow digits, operators, parentheses, decimal points, and whitespace. | If injection occurs, sanitize input and reject invalid characters. |
 227|| Slow evaluation for complex expressions | low | medium | Implement O(n) shunting-yard algorithm and set a timeout of 1 second. | If timeout exceeded, terminate evaluation and return error. |
 228|| Memory blowup for long inputs | low | medium | Use streaming tokenization and limit input length to 1000 characters. | If memory usage exceeds limit, implement memory monitoring and abort. |
 229|| Recursion depth exhaustion | low | high | Use iterative parsing (shunting-yard) instead of recursive descent. | If recursion depth exceeded, catch exception and return error. |
 230|

 237|- The GUI or CLI interface will be developed separately and will call the calculator engine.

preconditions: System is running and ready for input.

constraints.description: Input string length must not exceed 1000 characters.

risk_assessment.risk: Expression injection attack: malicious user could attempt to inject code through the expression input.

risk_assessment.contingency: Implement input validation and reject any non-mathematical characters.

risk_assessment.risk: Integer overflow: very large numbers could cause overflow or performance issues.
risk_assessment.mitigation: Set input length limit (1000 chars). Use Python's arbitrary precision integers.
risk_assessment.contingency: Catch overflow errors and display appropriate message.

risk_assessment.risk: Denial of service via complex expression: deeply nested parentheses or extremely long expressions could cause stack overflow or excessive CPU usage.

risk_assessment.contingency: Implement timeout for evaluation.

risk_assessment.risk: Floating point precision errors: floating point arithmetic may produce unexpected results (e.g., 0.1 + 0.2 = 0.30000000000000004).
risk_assessment.mitigation: Format output to 2 decimal places. Use Decimal for critical calculations if needed.
risk_assessment.contingency: Round result to two decimal places.

risk_assessment.risk: Security risk - unvalidated input: input may contain malicious content.
risk_assessment.mitigation: Sanitize input to allow only allowed characters.
risk_assessment.contingency: Reject any input containing disallowed characters.

assumptions: The calculator will be used in a trusted environment where users are not intentionally malicious.
The input expressions are in infix notation.
The maximum input length of 1000 characters is sufficient for typical use cases.
The system will be implemented in Python 3.8 or later.

use_cases.name: Complex Expression with Parentheses
preconditions: User has access to the calculator interface.
main_flow: 1. User enters an expression with parentheses (e.g., '(2+3)*4').
3. System evaluates respecting operator precedence and parentheses.
4. System displays the result formatted to 2 decimal places.
postconditions: User sees the correct result or an error message.
business_rules: Parentheses must be balanced.

use_cases.name: Division by Zero
preconditions: User has access to the calculator interface.
main_flow: 1. User enters an expression with division by zero (e.g., '5/0').

constraints.description: The system must be implemented in Python.
No use of eval() or exec() for expression evaluation.
Maximum input length is 1000 characters.
Result must be formatted to two decimal places.

risk_assessment.risk: Code injection via eval()
risk_assessment.mitigation: Use a custom parser (shunting-yard algorithm) instead of eval(). Validate all input characters before processing.
risk_assessment.contingency: If eval() is accidentally used, conduct code review and replace with safe parser.

risk_assessment.risk: Denial of Service via long input
risk_assessment.mitigation: Enforce a maximum input length of 1000 characters. Implement timeout for expression evaluation.
risk_assessment.contingency: If DoS occurs, restart the service and monitor input patterns.

risk_assessment.risk: Recursive parsing overflow
risk_assessment.mitigation: Use iterative parsing (shunting-yard) instead of recursive descent. Limit nesting depth to 100 levels.
risk_assessment.contingency: If stack overflow occurs, switch to iterative algorithm.

risk_assessment.risk: Slow tokenization for large inputs
risk_assessment.mitigation: Use a single-pass tokenizer with O(n) complexity. Avoid regex-based tokenization for performance-critical paths.
risk_assessment.contingency: Optimize tokenizer if performance issues arise.

risk_assessment.risk: Floating point precision issues
risk_assessment.mitigation: Use Decimal type for intermediate calculations where precision matters. Format final output to 2 decimal places.
risk_assessment.contingency: If precision errors are reported, switch to Decimal for all calculations.

risk_assessment.risk: Memory allocation for token storage
risk_assessment.mitigation: Use a streaming tokenizer that yields tokens one at a time. Limit maximum token count to 5000.
risk_assessment.contingency: If memory issues occur, implement token streaming.

assumptions: The calculator will be used in a single-user environment.
Input expressions will be in standard infix notation.
The system will not need to handle scientific notation or functions like sin, cos.
The user interface will be either command-line or GUI, but the core logic is independent of UI.
The system will run on a standard modern computer with sufficient resources.

project_summary.name: Python Calculator Application
project_summary.description: A Python-based calculator that evaluates string mathematical expressions with basic arithmetic operations (+, -, *, /), operator precedence, and parentheses support. It handles errors gracefully and returns results formatted to two decimal places. The calculator implements a safe expression parser without using eval() to prevent code injection.
project_summary.target_users: End users who need to perform basic arithmetic calculations via command-line or programmatic interface.
business_goals: Provide a safe and reliable calculator that prevents code injection attacks.
Ensure fast evaluation of expressions with response time under 100ms.
Deliver clear error messages in Chinese for usability.

risk_assessment.mitigation: Thoroughly test tokenizer with edge cases including leading minus, multiple decimals, etc.
risk_assessment.contingency: Add specific error messages for common tokenization errors.

assumptions: The calculator is used in a single-user environment (no concurrent requests).

 155|  7. 7. System displays the result to the user.

 163|    - 2b. Return to step 1.
 164|  - When If nesting depth exceeds limit:
 165|    - 4a. System rejects input with message '括号嵌套过深'.
 166|    - 4b. Return to step 1.
